message.content:
Here are some of the most popular and highly regarded sushi restaurants in Tokyo, ranging from Michelin‑starred establishments to well‑known local favorites:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights | Michelin Stars |
|------------|----------|------------|----------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (original) & Roppongi | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; famed for meticulous nigiri and a 3‑star Michelin rating (though the original Ginza location closed in 2017). | 3 |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | Intimate 8‑seat setting, renowned for precision and freshness; 3‑star Michelin. | 3 |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | Elegant, minimalist décor; 3‑star Michelin; focuses on seasonal ingredients. | 3 |
| **Sushi Mizutani** | Ginza | 3‑star Michelin; known for its “sushi of the day” concept and impeccable service. | 3 |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Famous for long lines but worth it for fresh tuna and sashimi. | N/A |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations (Shibuya, Shinjuku, etc.) | Casual, open‑air counter; great value for a wide variety of rolls and nigiri. | N/A |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic sushi experience; 2‑star Michelin; offers a “sushi of the day” menu. | 2 |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Ginza | 2‑star Michelin; known for its “sushi of the day” and high‑quality fish. | 2 |
| **Sushi Tsubaki** | Ginza | 2‑star Michelin; offers a refined tasting menu and a quiet atmosphere. | 2 |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Ginza | 1‑star Michelin; praised for its fresh fish and traditional techniques. | 1 |
| **Sushi Kanda** | Minato | 3‑star Michelin; small, intimate setting with a focus on seasonal ingredients. | 3 |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | 3‑star Michelin; known for its meticulous preparation and high quality. | 3 |
| **Sushi Shun** | Ginza | 1‑star Michelin; offers a modern take on classic sushi. | 1 |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Ginza | 2‑star Michelin; known for its “sushi of the day” and high‑quality fish. | 2 |

### Tips for Visiting

- **Reservations:** For Michelin‑starred spots, book months in advance. Many require a deposit or a credit card reservation.
- **Dress Code:** Some high‑end restaurants have a dress code; check ahead.
- **Tipping:** Not customary in Japan; excellent service is expected as part of the dining experience.
- **Payment:** Credit cards are accepted at many places, but some smaller establishments may only take cash.

Enjoy your sushi adventure in Tokyo!
